classification.difficultyReason: Construct midpoint segments to establish the specified median ratios, reuse that argument to prove concurrency, then connect equal medians through centroid ratios, isosceles angles and SAS congruence. The sequential parts scaffold the essential proof connections.

inlines.text: In this question we will prove that:
The medians of a triangle are concurrent and divide one another in the ratio 2:1.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let the medians $BE$ and $CF$ meet at $G$. Show that $BG=2GE$ and $CG=2GF$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with midpoint E on AC and midpoint F on AB; medians BE and CF meet at a red point G. Single ticks identify AE=EC and double ticks identify AF=FB.
spec.mathematics: E and F are midpoints. G is the intersection of BE and CF.
spec.answerVisibility: FE and ratio conclusions are absent from the question diagram.

answer.short:
$BG=2GE$ and $CG=2GF$.

Join $FE$. The midpoint theorem and $\triangle FGE\sim\triangle CGB$ give the ratio $1:2$.
answer.worked:
Join $FE$. Since $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of $AC$ and $AB$, the midpoint theorem gives $FE\parallel BC$ and $BC=2FE$.

In triangles $FGE$ and $CGB$, $\angle FGE=\angle CGB$ (vertically opposite angles) and $\angle GFE=\angle GCB$ (alternate angles, $FE\parallel BC$). Hence $\triangle FGE\sim\triangle CGB$ (AAA).
$$\begin{align*}\frac{CG}{GF}&=\frac{BC}{FE}=2\\\frac{BG}{GE}&=\frac{BC}{FE}=2\\CG&=2GF\\BG&=2GE\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$AD$ passes through $G$.

The same midpoint-and-similarity argument gives the same $2:1$ division point on $CF$.
answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $AD$ meet $CF$ at $G'$. Join $FD$. By the midpoint theorem, $FD\parallel AC$ and $AC=2FD$.

In triangles $AG'C$ and $DG'F$, $\angle AG'C=\angle DG'F$ (vertically opposite angles) and $\angle ACG'=\angle DFG'$ (alternate angles, $AC\parallel FD$). Hence $\triangle AG'C\sim\triangle DG'F$ (AAA).
$$\begin{align*}\frac{CG'}{G'F}&=\frac{AC}{DF}=2\\CG'&=2G'F\end{align*}$$
Part (a) gives $CG=2GF$. There is only one point dividing $CF$ internally in the ratio $2:1$, so $G'=G$. Therefore $AD$ also passes through $G$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that if two of the medians of a triangle have equal length, then the triangle is isosceles.

answer.short:
If $BE=CF$, then $AB=AC$, so $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles.

Use the centroid ratios to obtain $BG=CG$, then prove $\triangle BCF\cong\triangle CBE$ by SAS.
answer.worked:
Suppose the equal medians are $BE$ and $CF$. By part (a),
$$\begin{align*}BG&=\frac23BE\\CG&=\frac23CF\\BG&=CG\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle BGC$ is isosceles, so $\angle BCG=\angle CBG$. Since $C,G,F$ are collinear and $B,G,E$ are collinear, $\angle BCF=\angle CBE$.

In triangles $BCF$ and $CBE$, $BC=CB$ (common side), $CF=BE$ (given) and $\angle BCF=\angle CBE$. Hence $\triangle BCF\cong\triangle CBE$ (SAS), so $BF=CE$.

Since $F$ and $E$ are midpoints,
$$\begin{align*}AB&=2BF\\AC&=2CE\\AB&=AC\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles. The same argument applies whichever pair of medians is equal.
